summary: Configured native Alpine log rotation for `/var/log/inventory/app.log`: daily rotation, seven gzip-compressed archives, and `copytruncate` writer continuity. Scheduling and data survived the mandatory node restart; Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Installed Alpine-compatible logrotate 3.22.0 without upgrading the operating system or kernel.
Enabled and started BusyBox crond; Alpine's daily maintenance runs at 02:00.
Forced a controlled rotation while a writer held the log open, proving it could write afterward through the same inode.
Safely restarted node1 and verified its new boot identity, recovered scheduler, configuration, active log, and compressed archive.

evidence.requirement: Rotate daily and retain seven compressed rotations
evidence.summary: Configuration and debug output show a one-day interval and seven rotations; cron invokes daily maintenance; the controlled run created and validated a gzip archive.

evidence.requirement: Allow the application to continue writing after rotation
evidence.summary: The active log retained inode 65543 across rotation, and the same pre-opened writer successfully appended after rotation.

evidence.requirement: Keep the installed OS release and kernel
evidence.summary: Before and after changes/restart, the node reports Alpine 3.23.3 and kernel 6.18.7-0-lts.

Healthy baseline used boot ID 436837c0-0ffd-413c-aa81-0cbe806b3ed1; reboot was acknowledged; post-restart boot ID changed to bed9db70-6339-4bfa-8770-ae9b0641aac1; crond, policy, schedule, active data, rotation state, and valid compressed archive all recovered.
